Solid Italian, no gimmicks. Great night.

Ka'teen made a great impression from the moment we arrived. We were greeted warmly at the front, and since we had a reservation, we were seated right away. It was our first visit, and our server took the time to explain the menu, offer recommendations, and answer our questions without making us feel rushed.

One detail that really stood out was being asked if we were celebrating anything special. We mentioned it was my birthday, and the staff made the evening feel even more memorable with their thoughtful hospitality.

The atmosphere is beautiful. Between the lush greenery, warm lighting, and stylish décor, it feels like you've escaped the city for the evening. It has a tropical energy that reminded my son of Miami, while my wife and I couldn't help but think of the vibrant restaurants in Mexico City. Since it was a cool night, we also appreciated the outdoor heaters and blankets, which made the patio incredibly comfortable.

The food was every bit as impressive as the setting. Each dish was colorful, beautifully plated, and packed with flavors that felt fresh and unexpected. The crab enchiladas were easily the standout of the meal—rich, balanced, and absolutely delicious.

The relaxed, welcoming atmosphere made the whole experience even better. We ended up chatting with nearby tables, sharing recommendations, and already talking about what we'd order on our next visit before we had even finished dinner.

Valet parking was $17 for a couple of hours, which is pretty standard for the area. Between the outstanding service, unique food, and inviting ambiance, Ka'teen is definitely a place we'll be coming back to.

Such a hidden gem in Hollywood! From the moment you walk in, Laya feels like you’ve been transported into an open-air Middle Eastern market. The space is absolutely beautiful, with warm ambient lighting, a fire pit, a live DJ, and such an intimate, lively atmosphere.
I came here with my cousin who was visiting from Malaysia for a girls’ night, and we had such a wonderful experience. The staff was incredibly warm, hospitable, and attentive, and they truly made us feel so special throughout the evening.
For food, we started with the charred beetroot hummus and heirloom tomato salad. I’m usually not the biggest fan of beets, but the beetroot hummus completely surprised me — it was creamy, flavorful, and so delicious. The tomato salad was light, fresh, and refreshing. For our mains, we had the grilled branzino and wagyu beef shawarma, and both were so flavorful. We ended with the rose soft serve with pistachio and cotton candy, which was such a fun and beautiful way to finish the meal.
Laya is one of those restaurants where the atmosphere is just as memorable as the food. Such a great spot for a date night, girls’ night, or special occasion. We absolutely loved our experience and can’t wait to come back!

Perfect dinner date night spot in Hollywood. Good location central to a lot of great spots, with both valet and street parking options. Great service and friendly staff who were welcoming and allowed us to easily transfer our bar tab over to our dinner bill. We tried the Heart of the Desert and the Leavened Old Fashioned, refreshing and delicious. The ambiance was great, with a live violin player making the rounds.

For dinner we got the mixed kebab platter, which was a great sampling of what they have to offer. All delicious, but I have to give it to the WAGYU BEEF KEBAB! Never had anything like it. SO TASTY!!!  The Shish Tawouk (chicken) was also seasoned and cooked to perfection - if I only got two things next time it would be these. The bread was warm and tasty, the sauces were great, grilled veggies rounded everything out - loved it. We also tried the Batejan (eggplant) and Falafel Salad. Both were great, well cooked, and we really liked the dressing on the salad. Loved our meal, and we even decided to try two desserts - the chocolate molten lava cake which was baked to perfection and a really fun Rosé Cotton Candy + Pistachio ice cream dessert.

We will definitely return to have our favorite kebabs and to try more of the menu. Many more things we want to explore!

We’re visiting Los Angeles from Sydney, and starting our trip with dinner at Laya Restaurant has set the bar incredibly high. Everything about the experience was beyond amazing, from the food to the service.

We started with the Fried Kibbeh, which was perfectly crisp on the outside and packed with flavour inside. The spiced minced beef with burghul, hummus, and pickled red onion was an incredible combination.

The Batata Harra was another standout, triple cooked potatoes with garlic, Fresno chile, and cilantro. Crispy, spicy, and completely addictive.

For the main we shared the Mix Grill Platter, which was phenomenal. The Wagyu beef kebab, shish tawouk, and kafta khashkhash were all cooked perfectly, and the charred vegetables, pickled cucumber, parsley pesto, tomato chile, and toum made every bite even better.

The cocktails were so good we ended up ordering three rounds.
The Heart of the Desert, with tequila, prickly pear, strawberry, elderflower, and lime, was refreshing and beautifully balanced.
The Ambrosia, with gin, honeydew, coconut, elderflower, and pistachio, was unique and absolutely delicious.

For dessert we had the Chocolate Lava Cake and the Rose Soft Serve with pistachio, rose, and cotton candy, which was the perfect sweet finish.

What truly elevated the whole experience was the exceptional service, warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

An unforgettable meal and the perfect way to start our LA trip. We will absolutely be recommending Laya to everyone visiting Los Angeles.

Solid 💯

text.text:
Fabulous dining experience and exquisite food! We discovered the restaurant from the Eater youtube video about Gwen, which got us excited about the level of craftsmanship in the food. The actual experience far surpassed what we even expected after watching! We typically don’t like the Michelin restaurants that are too fine dining and try conceptual flavors. Gwen is nothing like that. Flavors are delicious, portions are large, you feel welcome as soon as you enter.

First the ambiance - it’s dark, moody, a little loud, open wood fired kitchen. We got sat upstairs which felt like a prohibition era speakeasy, already off to a great start.

All the food we ordered (listed below) was absolutely incredible, 10/10 on flavor and preparation. Favorites had to be the crudo, lamb ribs, corn pasta, and of course the ribeye. Everything was cooked to perfection, great texture, and again, just amazing flavor.

The service was also very attentive and you can tell they put a lot of pride in their work. They were easy to talk to, we made jokes together, they knew the menu like the back of their hand. But here’s what sets Gwen apart, if I could give 6/5 stars I would:

- they give you an amuse bouche, ours was a delicious tomato gazpacho with an herby oil, so refreshing and perfectly sweet/tangy.
- they let you choose your steak knife. We ordered the 36oz bone in ribeye off the special meat menu, and then the server came by with a closed wooden box, opened it and told us to each choose a knife, after which he would reveal their individual stories. It felt out of an adventure book! So we each selected and he proceeded to explain what they were made of, the brand, and special fun facts. Seriously elevated the experience, I’d bring back anyone you want to impress or have a good time: a date, family’s in town, your boss or a client.
- they finish the meal with a small tin of smoked salts made in house, as a takeaway token. We can’t wait to use them on a steak at home!

I can’t rave enough about Gwen. If you’ve been questioning whether to go, this is your sign to book the next available reservation.

- the best crusty but soft bread and butter
- amuse bouche gazpacho
- finishing salts at end of meal

- garganelli corn pasta
- Busiate sausage and kale pasta
- 36oz bone in ribeye
- duck fat potatoes
- wax beans
- the banana passionfruit dessert
- the chocolate caramel dessert

My only recommendation to staff: half way through meal a different waiter started waiting on us. Neither the first waiter announced his leaving, nor the second announced her takeover, which would have been appreciated.

From the moment we walked into Gwen’s, we knew we were in for something special. The filet mignon was absolutely outstanding—cooked to perfection and one of the best I’ve ever had.

What truly sets Gwen’s apart, though, is the service. Every staff member who passed our table seemed genuinely invested in making sure we had everything we needed. Empty dishes disappeared almost instantly, napkins were quietly refolded whenever we stepped away, and someone was always checking in without ever being intrusive. It’s first-class service that somehow still feels warm, comfortable, and homey—an incredibly difficult balance for any restaurant to achieve.

The highlight of the evening was when Chef Curtis Stone stopped by our table to ask how we were enjoying our meal. He was an absolute sweetheart and made us feel so welcome. Since we were celebrating my 66th birthday, he also surprised me with a beautifully boxed treat to take home, which was such a thoughtful touch.

At 66 years old, I’ve dined at countless restaurants, including many fine dining establishments, and I can honestly say this was my favorite dining experience. I’ve spent hundreds of dollars at other restaurants only to leave disappointed by the food or the service. At Gwen’s, every dollar was worth it. In fact, my husband—who usually has something to say about the bill—didn’t complain once. Instead, he couldn’t stop talking about how incredible the food and service were.

I had so many exceptional restaurants to choose from for my birthday celebration, and I am beyond grateful that I chose Gwen’s. It was an unforgettable evening, and we can’t wait to return.

Afterward, you can grab some tea or a cola to cut through the richness, and you’ll feel just fine.

Their people service is also good.

What this restaurant lacks in flavor, it makes up for in service. The atmosphere is beautiful, the music creates a great vibe, and every staff member we interacted with was kind, attentive, and knowledgeable.

Unfortunately, the food didn’t live up to the experience or the price. We ordered the half fried chicken (off menu), the Parkway, the snapper, and the kingfish, and none of the dishes impressed us. In fact, we didn’t finish any of them, which was especially disappointing considering our bill came to nearly $500. I also ordered the Carpe Verde cocktail, but it tasted more like a green smoothie than a cocktail. The complimentary celebration sorbet was a thoughtful touch, but it wasn’t to our taste either. The only thing we liked was the Calamari.

Parking was another frustration. There is essentially no dedicated parking. They offer valet for $20, but from what we experienced, it’s simply someone parking your car on the street for you. We also waited about 10 minutes for the valet while he was sitting in his own car before taking ours, which made the service feel difficult to justify.

I’d recommend this spot for drinks, appetizers, and the ambiance, but I wouldn’t return for dinner. At this price point, I expected a much more memorable dining experience.

Eat this cafe was the perfect treat for the end of a 3-day weekend. The weather was beautiful, and the bottomless mimosas were flowing. 2. Spicy chicken burrito: satisfying and flavorful chicken.
3. Eggs Benedict: a solid eggs benny.

We were beyond satisfied with our meal, and will be back for future weekend brunches!

Stopped in for the first time as a party of two for brunch on Friday and we both had a really nice meal. It’s a quick and casual little brunch and lunch spot that was even better than we were expecting. Our server was very polite and everything that we ordered came out pretty fast. They do have a good size menu with a lot of good options on it, there was more than I expected there to be. Inside is not very large, there aren’t many tables, but service is fast so I’m sure the tables turn quickly. I did not see any outside seating, it was all indoor. There is not a dedicated parking lot, street parking only. We found metered parking on the same block of the restaurant otherwise parking may be a bit tricky.

I started off a BBL, which is an iced coffee with brown sugar, banana syrup, and cinnamon. It was honestly really good and I would go back in there just for that alone. For my breakfast, I chose the Crab Cake Benedict and added avocado and really enjoyed it. The crabcakes were almost crispy and they had a lot of flavor to them which I really enjoyed. My eggs were cooked exactly as I ordered them and overall, I thought it was a really nice meal. It is a bit more expensive than I expected it to be, we did start with a pair of the Corn Ribs, which were a nice start but everything was just a little bit pricey. It was almost $90 for a party of two, but I do think it is worth it if you’re in the area and stop in on occasion.
